shared_elements: low-relief carving on a tall rectangular upright slab face
glyphs organised in rows and columns forming a grid
a horizontal band of glyph blocks
flat, shallow relief with rounded raised forms
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow relief composed of rounded-square, densely packed sign blocks arranged in aligned rows and columns, a fairly specific convention shared between them (visible in A's basal band and vertical column). The decisive difference is the composition: A is dominated by a large central figural/iconic panel with the script relegated to a narrow band, whereas B is an unbroken all-over field of script with no figure at all.
